need.rule: Citizens of countries on the EU's visa list need this visa. Everyone else can visit the Schengen area for up to 90 days in any 180 days without one.
notes: The EU's planned online travel permit for visa-free visitors (ETIAS) is not running yet, and no start date has been announced.

checker.label: The EU's list of who needs a visa

items.label: Adults and children aged 12 and over

fees.note: The same in every Schengen country. A visa centre (such as VFS or TLS) may add its own service fee.

source.label: German Federal Foreign Office: Schengen visa fee

time.text: Usually decided within 15 calendar days after the consulate accepts your application. It can take up to 45 days if they need to check more.

source.label: EU Visa Code, article 23 (Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

coverage.text: Ta'asheera asks you every question in plain language, checks your answers and lists your documents. It can also fill in the official Schengen application PDF for you to print, and its agent can type your answers into the Schengen online form (tested on a practice copy of the form). The agent always stops before the declaration: you check everything and submit it yourself.

need.rule: Citizens of countries on the UK's visa list need this visa. Most other visitors need an electronic travel authorisation (ETA) instead, which they apply for online.

checker.label: GOV.UK: Check if you need a UK visa

items.label: Long-term visa, 2 years (6 months per visit)

fees.note: Fees are not refunded if the visa is refused.

source.label: GOV.UK: Apply for a Standard Visitor visa

time.text: Usually about 3 weeks after your appointment at the visa application centre.

coverage.text: Ta'asheera asks you every question in plain language, checks your answers and lists your documents. You then fill in the official online form on GOV.UK yourself, using your saved answers.

need.rule: Citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries can usually visit for up to 90 days with an ESTA instead of a visa. Everyone else needs a visitor visa (B-2).

checker.label: US Customs and Border Protection: Visa Waiver Program

fees.note: Paid before the interview and not refunded. Some US embassies also charge a $250 visa integrity fee when the visa is issued; not every embassy charges it yet, so check with yours.

source.label: US Department of State: Fees for visa services

time.text: There is no fixed time: it depends on how long you wait for an interview at your embassy, from a few days to many months.

source.label: US Department of State: Visa appointment wait times

coverage.text: Ta'asheera asks you every question in plain language, checks your answers and lists your documents. You then fill in the official DS-160 form yourself, using your saved answers, and go to the interview.

extra_sources.label: Boston University international office: Visa integrity fee

need.rule: Most travellers need either a visitor visa or an electronic travel authorization (eTA), not both. Which one depends on your passport.

checker.label: IRCC: Find out if you need a visa

fees.note: Biometrics cost at most CAD 170 for a family applying together.

time.text: It depends on the country you apply from, from a couple of weeks to several months.

coverage.text: Ta'asheera asks you every question in plain language, checks your answers and lists your documents. You then apply online in your IRCC account yourself, using your saved answers, and give your biometrics.
